title: terraform: private deploy - modularize GPU node pools, IAM roles, networking, and remote state layout
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: stabilize private deployment Terraform for GPU-based private clusters and reduce blast radius during upgrades by modularizing node pools, clearly scoping IAM resources, and introducing a standardized remote state layout. This PR splits the monolithic cluster module into: modules/gpu-node-pool (per-GPU-type node pools with autoscaling and taints), modules/iam (node instance roles, service account bindings with least privilege), and modules/network (vpc/subnet/peerings). It also introduces a new recommended remote state layout (backend.tf and state/README.md) which stores state per-environment and per-module to enable safe partial plans and unlockable upgrades across regions. The description includes migration steps for existing customers and infra teams: 1) backend migration plan using terraform state mv commands outlined in state/README.md; 2) create per-module state buckets and DynamoDB locks (AWS) or per-project GCS buckets (GCP); 3) validate with the included examples/private-deploy and run terratest e2e to ensure node pools and IAM policies apply correctly. Design decisions: keep GPU node pool module provider-agnostic with AWS/GKE/AKS flags, expose node role override for customer-managed instance profiles, and default to separate instance profile per node pool to allow safe rolling upgrades. Testing: added unit-level plan checks in ci/terraform-plan.yml and terratest integration under tests/private-deploy. Backwards-compatibility: the default behavior preserves existing cluster resource names; however the state layout change requires the manual migration steps documented. Checklist: [x] split modules and add variables with clear defaults, [x] backend state layout and migration guide, [x] unit and integration CI updates, [x] docs/upgrade.md with steps, [x] security review for IAM least-privilege. Impact: reduces plan churn when modifying node pools, enables per-nodepool rollout and rollback, and resolves race conditions seen when multiple engineers apply changes concurrently.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Please split the node role from the node pool module so that customers with custom instance profiles can pass them without TF recreates. Also add lifecycle.ignore_changes for node labels.
Author (Aisha Khan): Split node role into modules/iam and added node_role_override var with example in examples/private-deploy. Added lifecycle block for node labels per Diego's suggestion.
Lena Schultz: We need a clear migration path for existing state. Can you add steps and a small script example? Also ensure DynamoDB lock table TTL config is explicit.

Author (Aisha Khan): Added state/README.md with explicit terraform state mv commands, S3/GCS examples, and a helper migration script in state/migrate.sh. DynamoDB section documents recommended read/write capacity and TTL settings.
Omar Patel: CI failed on terraform fmt on first run. After fixes, please re-run terratest in CI to validate node creation on the smallest GPU instance type. Approving after green CI.
Author (Aisha Khan): Fixed formatting and reduced test footprint by running terratest with mocked providers for unit CI and a single region e2e smoke test. CI passing now.
release_notes: Modularized Terraform for private deployments: GPU node pools extracted to a dedicated module, IAM roles separated for least-privilege and customer overrides, networking module improvements, and a new recommended remote state layout with migration guide. This reduces plan blast radius and enables safer node pool upgrades. Follow docs/upgrade.md and state/README.md to migrate existing state.
